tasks.title: Optimize useModalFocus to prevent UI freeze during Tab navigation in large lists
acceptance: Pressing Tab in a modal with thousands of items evaluates style for only a few elements, not all of them
Focus correctly cycles between the first and last available focusable elements
Shift+Tab correctly navigates backwards from the first element to the last element

evidence.detail: Measured performance of useModalFocus using a jsdom synthetic test with 10,000 items. The current implementation iterates through all items, calling window.getComputedStyle on each. Switching to short-circuiting array methods (.find and .findLast) significantly reduces style computations from 10,000 to a constant number depending on visibility.

steps: Open the Codex import modal and load a list with thousands of items
Press the Tab key to cycle focus
reproduction.expected: Focus moves to the next focusable element quickly, avoiding O(N) synchronous style computations
reproduction.actual: The UI performs O(N) style computations, causing a noticeable UI freeze during keyboard navigation

revisit.difference: The previous proposal sought to virtualize the entire list, introducing significant layout complexity to address a rendering stress case. This new proposal targets a completely distinct algorithmic bottleneck: an O(N) loop of synchronous getComputedStyle layout queries during keyboard navigation (Tab), which is resolved with a simple array method change (.find vs .findLast) without altering the layout.

responses.why_previous_reason_no_longer_explains: The rejection highlighted the layout complexity of virtualization and the lack of native-user lag for rendering. This new proposal does not virtualize the list or change any layout logic, thus avoiding the layout complexity entirely. It exclusively optimizes an O(N) keyboard event handler to use short-circuiting, a minimal algorithmic change.

proposal_decision.note: Resolved externally in merged PR #95 (https://github.com/Omnividente/omp-desktop/pull/95, main d659001d1ec8a70fa982b88ce77de1e9c8621544): useModalFocus.ts avoids per-Tab full-control style computations. Windows/Linux quality gates and targeted regression checks passed.

research_result.summary: Verified hypotheses for ModelPicker keyboard handling, SettingsRecoveryScreen ARIA/focus, and ModelPicker performance latency.

observations.scenario: Handling the Enter key within the ModelPicker search and manual inputs.
observations.evidence: Tested rendering ModelPicker in a Vitest jsdom environment. Dispatched a 'keydown' event with key 'Enter' on both search and manual inputs. In both cases, the picker was not closed and no selection occurred.
observations.result: Establishes that the Enter key is currently ignored in both inputs, and should be handled to improve keyboard navigation.

observations.scenario: Checking ARIA roles and auto-focus behavior on SettingsRecoveryScreen.
observations.evidence: Tested rendering SettingsRecoveryScreen in a Vitest jsdom environment. Checked for the `role` attribute on the container and inspected `document.activeElement` after rendering. Neither `role="alertdialog"` was present nor focus was placed on the primary button.
observations.result: Establishes that the recovery screen lacks the alertdialog role and auto-focus on the primary action button, degrading accessibility.

observations.scenario: Measuring filtering performance with 5000 models in ModelPicker.
observations.evidence: Rendered ModelPicker with 5000 synthetic models in Vitest jsdom. Triggering an `onChange` event with a search string takes significantly long time (around 2 seconds) due to repeated string array joining inside the filtering loop.
observations.result: Establishes that string allocations during filtering introduce noticeable latency, which should be optimized by pre-calculating search terms.

next_hypotheses: Investigate if virtualizing the listbox options using `react-window` or `react-virtuoso` further reduces DOM layout thrashing.
Investigate if fallback chains selection needs better validation to handle empty missing models.

previous_reports.summary: Measured ModelPicker rendering and filtering performance with a large model set. Identified significant latency in query updates and selection mapping.

observations.scenario: Filtering and rendering a synthetic payload of 5000 models in the ModelPicker.
observations.evidence: Tested rendering ModelPicker in a Vitest jsdom environment with 5000 models. Changing the query from an empty string to 'Model 499' timed out tests configured at default thresholds. Isolated benchmarking of the `filteredModels` useMemo block and the `matchesSelector` check inside the render loop showed that repeatedly splitting and joining strings (`[model.name, model.provider, model.id, model.selector].join(' ').toLowerCase()`) and recalculating `splitSelector` takes ~218ms and ~110ms respectively.
observations.result: Establishes that string allocations during filtering and selection mapping introduce noticeable latency, which can be optimized by caching search terms and hoisting the `splitSelector` calculation out of the map.

next_hypotheses: Investigate if virtualizing the listbox options using `react-window` or `react-virtuoso` further reduces DOM layout thrashing.

previous_reports.summary: Verified that virtual scrolling handles continuous wheel scrolling and large scroll jumps across drastically varied row heights without introducing unhandled jitter or layout flickers.

observations.scenario: Continuous mouse-wheel scrolling in `useVirtualList` with drastically varying row heights (alternating between 50px and 2000px).
observations.evidence: Isolated test rendering `useVirtualList` directly, artificially updating scroll bounds simulating wheel events with drastically different mocked heights. Verified via observed internal `scrollTop` events and resulting `virtualItems` that `useVirtualList` accurately anchors and updates offset locations without entering cyclic scroll position adjustments.
observations.result: Establishes that the virtual list handles severe row height variations smoothly during continuous scroll interactions without layout artifacts or scroll jitter.

observations.scenario: Jumping between far apart search matches in `TranscriptModal` using Next/Prev navigation when target rows are offscreen and have different heights.
observations.evidence: Tested `TranscriptModal` component via `jsdom` with mock elements configured to report bounding clients far apart. Clicking the Next Match button successfully caused `scrollToIndex` to mount the offscreen virtual row and subsequently `requestAnimationFrame` adjusted the intra-element `scrollTop` correctly using the new target bounds, avoiding visual flicker.
observations.result: Establishes that `TranscriptModal` accurately reconciles layout constraints and smoothly lands on the target matches even when they require complex layout invalidation from unmeasured elements.

next_hypotheses: Investigate if focusing the content action menu immediately after changing a transcript view mode disrupts screen reader announcements for the new view state.
Investigate the accessibility of the `MarkdownContent` code block copy buttons when navigating strictly by keyboard.

previous_reports.summary: Investigated keyboard accessibility and screen reader support for copy buttons, transcript state containers, and mode toggles in the TranscriptModal.

observations.scenario: Navigating to code block copy buttons via keyboard and screen reader.
observations.evidence: Ran isolated jsdom Vitest checks on `MarkdownContent` containing code blocks. The `.markdown-copy-button` button renders correctly in tab order (tabIndex=0 by default for `<button>`), and has explicit `aria-label="Copy code"` with `title="Copy code"` (or `aria-label="Copy text"` for general messages). When clicked, the inner span successfully dynamically updates with `role="status"` and `aria-live="polite"` via React state.
observations.result: Establishes that code block copy buttons and general message copy buttons are fully keyboard accessible and correctly announce copied state changes dynamically without losing focus.

observations.scenario: Changing transcript view mode via the transcript filter buttons.
observations.evidence: Ran isolated jsdom Vitest checks simulating a click on the 'Dialogue + service' button while focused. The active focus remains on the clicked mode button, correctly retaining its layout in the toolbar without dropping focus back to `document.body`.
observations.result: Establishes that changing transcript view modes does not disrupt keyboard navigation state or drop focus.

observations.scenario: Evaluating empty/error/no-match transcript state screen reader announcements.
observations.evidence: Ran isolated jsdom Vitest checks capturing the HTML of `.transcript-state` containers under different conditions. Observed that the 'Error' and 'Loading' states correctly include `role="alert"` and `aria-live="polite"` respectively. However, the 'Empty' state (`<div className="transcript-state">`) and 'No Matches' state (`<div className="transcript-state">`) lack `role="status"` and `aria-live="polite"` attributes entirely in `TranscriptModal.tsx`.
observations.result: Establishes that while errors and loading states announce properly, screen reader users might miss changes if a transcript is successfully emptied or a search yields zero matches, because the state block acts as a standard static `div`.

next_hypotheses: Investigate if long external links within inline text elements are fully readable to screen readers without excessive unpronounceable token reading.
Investigate the accessibility of keyboard focus flow when pressing `Escape` to close the `ContentActionMenu` from an internal link context menu.

previous_reports.summary: Verified that pressing Escape to close the ContentActionMenu restores keyboard focus correctly when triggered from an internal link context menu.

observations.scenario: Opening the internal link context menu in TranscriptModal and CompletedAnswers, navigating the menu via keyboard arrows, and pressing Escape.
observations.evidence: Tested using isolated jsdom Vitest checks on TranscriptModal and CompletedAnswers. In both cases, onLinkContextMenu records the currently focused element (the link) into `menu.focus`. ContentActionMenu manages focus internally using keydown event handlers. When Escape is pressed, it triggers `onDismiss(true)`. In TranscriptModal and CompletedAnswers, `dismissMenu(true)` successfully retrieves the stored `menu.focus` and restores keyboard focus directly back to the `<a>` element, preventing focus loss.
observations.result: Establishes that the keyboard focus flow correctly restores focus to the underlying link after the action menu is closed with Escape, preserving accessibility state.

next_hypotheses: Investigate if long external links within inline text elements are fully readable to screen readers without excessive unpronounceable token reading.

Then fired a `modelChange` event with `modelRole: "primary"` and `resolvedModelIsFallback: false`. `resolveFallbacks` checks `role === null ? incident.role === null : incident.role === role || incident.role === null`. Because the passed role is `"primary"` but the incident role is `"secondary"`, the active incident is skipped and remains active.
observations.result: Establishes a logical bug (hypothesis discovery-aa17322b78e9eae9) where returning to the primary model fails to clear an active secondary fallback incident. research_result.summary: Investigated the runtime incidents failure recovery and state bounding logic, verifying bugs where active fallbacks are prematurely dropped under high error volume, and secondary fallbacks fail to resolve when the primary model recovers. Also investigated focus trap bounds for nested details tags.

observations.scenario: Verify if `enforceIncidentBound` mistakenly drops unresolved primary fallback issues under a high volume of errors on the same terminal.
observations.evidence: Ran isolated tests on `enforceIncidentBound` by adding a fallback incident for `term1`, then generating 110 unique errors for the same terminal. Because `candidates` first filters by terminals with `> 1` active incidents before falling back to all active incidents, it selects the 100+ active errors on `term1` alongside the active fallback. The `reduce` step evicts the oldest incident, which is the still-active fallback. This was reproduced via a custom tsx script.
observations.result: Establishes a logical bug (hypothesis discovery-940b5f71f3979b02) where an active fallback is dropped from state if its terminal continuously emits errors. This hides the fallback health status from the UI.

observations.scenario: Verify if `resolveFallbacks` correctly resolves a secondary fallback on primary model recovery.
observations.evidence: Tested `applyRuntimeIncidentEvent` via a custom tsx script by creating a `retryFallbackApplied` incident with `fallbackRole: "secondary"`. Then fired a `modelChange` event with `modelRole: "primary"` and `resolvedModelIsFallback: false`. `resolveFallbacks` checks `role === null ? incident.role === null : incident.role === role || incident.role === null`. Because the passed role is `"primary"` but the incident role is `"secondary"`, the active incident is skipped and remains active.
observations.result: Establishes a logical bug (hypothesis discovery-aa17322b78e9eae9) where returning to the primary model fails to clear an active secondary fallback incident.

observations.scenario: Fix focus trap bound calculation for elements hidden inside collapsed details tags.
observations.evidence: Created a jsdom test to verify if elements inside collapsed `<details>` tags are ignored by the inline `DIALOG_FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR` query. The `.filter((element) => !element.hasAttribute("disabled") && !element.hidden)` check in `IncidentCenter` and `ResourceHealthPanel` does not exclude them, leading to broken Tab traversal.
observations.result: Establishes that the inline query must explicitly check for `!element.closest('details:not([open])')` while retaining `<summary>` tags to correctly replicate the `useModalFocus` behavior.

next_hypotheses: Investigate if `runtimeEventsDedupeKey` fails to coalesce rapid identical error events, exacerbating the bound exhaustion bug.

evidence.detail: Read-only scoped investigation; do not change product files or open a PR. Choose one user journey in this area; exercise a normal transition and a boundary input using isolated synthetic data. Compare frontend behavior with its backend contract and capture expected versus observed results. On a revisit choose a different journey or investigate a previous next_hypothesis; do not repeat a generic quality gate. Use isolated synthetic data, never live sessions or credentials. previous_reports.summary: Measured performance of incident bounding, diagnostics text redaction, and resource health sampling; no severe regressions or bottlenecks found.

observations.scenario: Continuous terminal state updates exceeding the MAX_RUNTIME_INCIDENTS limit, forcing `enforceIncidentBound` to continuously drop the oldest unique terminal event.
observations.evidence: Executed an isolated synthetic TypeScript benchmark with 10,000 incident insertions across 100+ unique terminals to force worst-case limit scaling. The O(N) array filtering and reduction to drop the oldest incident processed 10,000 boundary evictions in ~300ms (~0.03ms per event).
observations.result: Establishes that the incident limit tracking is well bounded in execution time and memory; the O(N) eviction behavior is not a measurable bottleneck due to the small N=100 hard limit.

observations.scenario: Resource-intensive text redaction over large chunks of textual data during diagnostics collection (`redact_text`).
observations.evidence: Wrote a native Rust benchmark `benchmark_redact_text` for `omp_desktop_lib::diagnostics::redact_text` simulating processing of 100,000 lines (2.5MB) containing secrets. Redaction completed in ~838ms.
observations.result: Establishes that `redact_text` is appropriately bounded; while line-by-line token splitting over millions of lines induces some latency, realistic diagnostic log sizes remain within acceptable sub-second limits.

observations.scenario: Live `sample_resource_health` retrieval performance.
observations.evidence: Wrote a native Rust benchmark `benchmark_resource_health` for `omp_desktop_lib::resource_health::sample_resource_health`. 10 successive live system resource samples completed in ~8.3ms.
observations.result: Establishes that continuous system telemetry retrieval executes efficiently (~0.8ms per sample) and does not incur expensive filesystem IO blocking.

next_hypotheses: Verify if concurrent high-throughput terminal outputs can cause overlapping `redact_text` invocations to block the Tauri IPC event loop when retrieving extremely large diagnostics logs.
Investigate the memory allocations required when serializing 100 active runtime incidents over the IPC bridge during intense terminal activity.

Because `candidates` first filters by terminals with `> 1` active incidents before falling back to all active incidents, it selects the 100+ active errors on `term1` alongside the active fallback. The `reduce` step evicts the oldest incident, which is the still-active fallback. Wait, it drops it even when it's unresolved.
observations.result: Establishes a logical bug (hypothesis discovery-940b5f71f3979b02) where an active fallback is dropped from state if its terminal continuously emits errors. This hides the fallback health status from the UI.

observations.scenario: Verify if `resolveFallbacks` correctly resolves a secondary fallback on primary model recovery.
observations.evidence: Tested `applyRuntimeIncidentEvent` by creating a `retryFallbackApplied` incident with `fallbackRole: "secondary"`. observations.scenario: Verify if `enforceIncidentBound` mistakenly drops unresolved primary fallback issues under a high volume of errors on the same terminal.
observations.evidence: Ran isolated tests on `enforceIncidentBound` by adding a fallback incident for `term1`, then generating 110 unique errors for the same terminal. Because `candidates` first filters by terminals with `> 1` active incidents before falling back to all active incidents, it selects the 100+ active errors on `term1` alongside the active fallback. observations.result: Establishes a logical bug (hypothesis discovery-940b5f71f3979b02) where an active fallback is dropped from state if its terminal continuously emits errors. This hides the fallback health status from the UI.

observations.scenario: Verify if `resolveFallbacks` correctly resolves a secondary fallback on primary model recovery.
observations.evidence: Tested `applyRuntimeIncidentEvent` via a custom tsx script by creating a `retryFallbackApplied` incident with `fallbackRole: "secondary"`. Then fired a `modelChange` event with `modelRole: "primary"` and `resolvedModelIsFallback: false`. `resolveFallbacks` checks `role === null ? incident.role === null : incident.role === role || incident.role === null`. Because the passed role is `"primary"` but the incident role is `"secondary"`, the active incident is skipped and remains active.
observations.result: Establishes a logical bug (hypothesis discovery-aa17322b78e9eae9) where returning to the primary model fails to clear an active secondary fallback incident.

observations.scenario: Fix focus trap bound calculation for elements hidden inside collapsed details tags.
observations.evidence: Created a jsdom test to verify if elements inside collapsed `<details>` tags are ignored by the inline `DIALOG_FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR` query. The `.filter((element) => !element.hasAttribute("disabled") && !element.hidden)` check in `IncidentCenter` and `ResourceHealthPanel` does not exclude them, leading to broken Tab traversal.
observations.result: Establishes that the inline query must explicitly check for `!element.closest('details:not([open])')` while retaining `<summary>` tags to correctly replicate the `useModalFocus` behavior.

previous_reports.summary: Measured performance of incident bounding, diagnostics text redaction, and resource health sampling; no severe regressions or bottlenecks found.

observations.scenario: Continuous terminal state updates exceeding the MAX_RUNTIME_INCIDENTS limit, forcing `enforceIncidentBound` to continuously drop the oldest unique terminal event.
observations.evidence: Executed an isolated synthetic TypeScript benchmark with 10,000 incident insertions across 100+ unique terminals to force worst-case limit scaling. The O(N) array filtering and reduction to drop the oldest incident processed 10,000 boundary evictions in ~300ms (~0.03ms per event).
observations.result: Establishes that the incident limit tracking is well bounded in execution time and memory; the O(N) eviction behavior is not a measurable bottleneck due to the small N=100 hard limit.

observations.scenario: Resource-intensive text redaction over large chunks of textual data during diagnostics collection (`redact_text`).
observations.evidence: Wrote a native Rust benchmark `benchmark_redact_text` for `omp_desktop_lib::diagnostics::redact_text` simulating processing of 100,000 lines (2.5MB) containing secrets. Redaction completed in ~838ms.
observations.result: Establishes that `redact_text` is appropriately bounded; while line-by-line token splitting over millions of lines induces some latency, realistic diagnostic log sizes remain within acceptable sub-second limits.

observations.scenario: Live `sample_resource_health` retrieval performance.
observations.evidence: Wrote a native Rust benchmark `benchmark_resource_health` for `omp_desktop_lib::resource_health::sample_resource_health`. 10 successive live system resource samples completed in ~8.3ms.
observations.result: Establishes that continuous system telemetry retrieval executes efficiently (~0.8ms per sample) and does not incur expensive filesystem IO blocking.

next_hypotheses: Verify if concurrent high-throughput terminal outputs can cause overlapping `redact_text` invocations to block the Tauri IPC event loop when retrieving extremely large diagnostics logs.
Investigate the memory allocations required when serializing 100 active runtime incidents over the IPC bridge during intense terminal activity.

previous_reports.summary: Investigated the runtime incidents failure recovery and state bounding logic, reproducing bugs where active fallbacks are prematurely dropped under high error volume, and secondary fallbacks fail to resolve when the primary model recovers.

observations.scenario: Verify if `enforceIncidentBound` mistakenly drops unresolved primary fallback issues under a high volume of errors on the same terminal.
observations.evidence: Ran isolated tests on `enforceIncidentBound` by adding a fallback incident for `term1`, then generating 110 unique errors for the same terminal. Because `candidates` first filters by terminals with `> 1` active incidents before falling back to all active incidents, it selects the 100+ active errors on `term1` alongside the active fallback. The `reduce` step evicts the oldest incident, which is the still-active fallback. Wait, it drops it even when it's unresolved.
observations.result: Establishes a logical bug (hypothesis discovery-940b5f71f3979b02) where an active fallback is dropped from state if its terminal continuously emits errors. This hides the fallback health status from the UI.

observations.scenario: Verify if `resolveFallbacks` correctly resolves a secondary fallback on primary model recovery.
observations.evidence: Tested `applyRuntimeIncidentEvent` by creating a `retryFallbackApplied` incident with `fallbackRole: "secondary"`. Then fired a `modelChange` event with `modelRole: "primary"` and `resolvedModelIsFallback: false`. `resolveFallbacks` checks `role === null ? incident.role === null : incident.role === role || incident.role === null`. Because the passed role is `"primary"` but the incident role is `"secondary"`, the active incident is skipped and remains active.
observations.result: Establishes a logical bug (hypothesis discovery-aa17322b78e9eae9) where returning to the primary model fails to clear an active secondary fallback incident. I verified this natively in vitest. Expanding the filter to `role === null ? true : incident.role === role || incident.role === null` broke unrelated tests by clearing unrelated roles like 'review', but modifying the default recovery logic (`role ?? "default"`) to target the specific target fallback roles correctly clears it.

next_hypotheses: Investigate the interaction between `fallbackRole`, `modelRole`, and the `resolveFallbacks` criteria when a review fallback overlaps with a primary fallback.

Verify the behavior of `IncidentCenter` when navigating through an arbitrary sequence of nested `<details>` elements containing errors, as `DIALOG_FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR` may skip focus boundaries incorrectly.

observations.result: Establishes a logical bug (hypothesis discovery-aa17322b78e9eae9) where returning to the primary model fails to clear an active secondary fallback incident.

observations.scenario: Fix focus trap bound calculation for elements hidden inside collapsed details tags.
observations.evidence: Created a jsdom test to verify if elements inside collapsed `<details>` tags are ignored by the inline `DIALOG_FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR` query. The `.filter((element) => !element.hasAttribute("disabled") && !element.hidden)` check in `IncidentCenter` and `ResourceHealthPanel` does not exclude them, leading to broken Tab traversal.
observations.result: Establishes that the inline query must explicitly check for `!element.closest('details:not([open])')` while retaining `<summary>` tags to correctly replicate the `useModalFocus` behavior.

IncidentCenter.tsx:129-133 намеренно отключает возврат к кнопке вызова панели; App.tsx:1168-1177,2304 выбирает нужную вкладку и увеличивает terminalFocusRequest для передачи фокуса терминалу. Возврат к старому trigger сломал бы смысл Open terminal. Mock callback без окружения App не доказывает ошибку сквозного перехода; новый report должен показать потерю фокуса в настоящем TerminalView. Нативную проверку сейчас не запускали.
decision_context.title: Restore focus correctly when IncidentCenter closes via 'Open terminal'

research_result.summary: Investigated the runtime incidents failure recovery state machine and focus trap bounds logic, verifying three separate bugs isolated under simulated test environments regarding unbounded fallback dropping, secondary fallback resolution failure, and ignored element attributes in focus queries.

observations.scenario: Verify if `enforceIncidentBound` mistakenly drops unresolved primary fallback issues under a high volume of errors on the same terminal.
observations.evidence: Ran an isolated state machine test `src/vitest_bug2.test.tsx` on `enforceIncidentBound` by adding a fallback incident for `terminal-1`, then applying 110 unique errors for the same terminal. The oldest active incident, which is the still-unresolved fallback, was mistakenly dropped from state to keep within `MAX_RUNTIME_INCIDENTS`, which subsequently alters `runtimeHealthStatus` to incorrectly return `error` instead of `fallback`.
observations.result: Establishes a logical bug where an active fallback is dropped from state if its terminal continuously emits errors. Verified previously proposed task `discovery-940b5f71f3979b02` using native jsdom environments.

observations.scenario: Verify if `resolveFallbacks` correctly resolves a secondary fallback on primary model recovery.
observations.evidence: Tested `applyRuntimeIncidentEvent` via a custom test script `src/vitest_bug2.test.tsx` by creating a `retryFallbackApplied` incident with `fallbackRole: "secondary"`. Then fired a `modelChange` event with `modelRole: "primary"` and `resolvedModelIsFallback: false`. The test output confirmed that the fallback incident remained in `status: "active"` instead of being resolved.
observations.result: Establishes a logical bug (hypothesis discovery-aa17322b78e9eae9) where returning to the primary model fails to clear an active secondary fallback incident because `resolveFallbacks` uses a strict equality check (`incident.role === role`) against "primary" which ignores "secondary".

observations.scenario: Verify focus trap bound calculation for elements hidden inside collapsed details tags.
observations.evidence: Created a jsdom test `src/vitest_bug.test.tsx` to mount `<IncidentCenter />` containing a `<details>` element which is closed by default. Mocked adding a `<button>` inside this details element. Simulating a Tab press via `userEvent` resulted in the focus trap's internal `document.activeElement` landing on the hidden "Inner Button" inside the closed details, breaking expected Tab traversal logic.
observations.result: Establishes that the inline query string `DIALOG_FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR` combined with `!element.hidden` does not correctly filter out DOM elements that are visibly hidden by being inside a collapsed `<details>` wrapper, corroborating task `discovery-8666a6b31891895740080f96baa815074d241d21013dc5c54b34a8818f65a4fe`.

next_hypotheses: Investigate if `runtimeEventsDedupeKey` fails to coalesce rapid identical error events, exacerbating the bound exhaustion bug.
Verify if concurrent high-throughput terminal outputs can cause overlapping `redact_text` invocations to block the Tauri IPC event loop when retrieving extremely large diagnostics logs.

previous_reports.summary: Investigated the runtime incidents failure recovery and state bounding logic, verifying bugs where active fallbacks are prematurely dropped under high error volume, and secondary fallbacks fail to resolve when the primary model recovers. Also investigated focus trap bounds for nested details tags.

observations.scenario: Verify if `enforceIncidentBound` mistakenly drops unresolved primary fallback issues under a high volume of errors on the same terminal.
observations.evidence: Ran isolated tests on `enforceIncidentBound` by adding a fallback incident for `term1`, then generating 110 unique errors for the same terminal. Because `candidates` first filters by terminals with `> 1` active incidents before falling back to all active incidents, it selects the 100+ active errors on `term1` alongside the active fallback. The `reduce` step evicts the oldest incident, which is the still-active fallback. This was reproduced via a custom tsx script.
observations.result: Establishes a logical bug (hypothesis discovery-940b5f71f3979b02) where an active fallback is dropped from state if its terminal continuously emits errors. This hides the fallback health status from the UI.

observations.scenario: Verify if `resolveFallbacks` correctly resolves a secondary fallback on primary model recovery.
observations.evidence: Tested `applyRuntimeIncidentEvent` via a custom tsx script by creating a `retryFallbackApplied` incident with `fallbackRole: "secondary"`. Then fired a `modelChange` event with `modelRole: "primary"` and `resolvedModelIsFallback: false`. `resolveFallbacks` checks `role === null ? incident.role === null : incident.role === role || incident.role === null`. Because the passed role is `"primary"` but the incident role is `"secondary"`, the active incident is skipped and remains active.
observations.result: Establishes a logical bug (hypothesis discovery-aa17322b78e9eae9) where returning to the primary model fails to clear an active secondary fallback incident.

observations.scenario: Fix focus trap bound calculation for elements hidden inside collapsed details tags.
observations.evidence: Created a jsdom test to verify if elements inside collapsed `<details>` tags are ignored by the inline `DIALOG_FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR` query. The `.filter((element) => !element.hasAttribute("disabled") && !element.hidden)` check in `IncidentCenter` and `ResourceHealthPanel` does not exclude them, leading to broken Tab traversal.
observations.result: Establishes that the inline query must explicitly check for `!element.closest('details:not([open])')` while retaining `<summary>` tags to correctly replicate the `useModalFocus` behavior.

next_hypotheses: Investigate if `runtimeEventsDedupeKey` fails to coalesce rapid identical error events, exacerbating the bound exhaustion bug.

previous_reports.summary: Verified focus trap bound calculation bug in IncidentCenter/ResourceHealthPanel and reproduced edge cases where unresolved fallbacks are dropped and secondary fallbacks fail to resolve.

observations.scenario: Focus trap logic inside IncidentCenter and ResourceHealthPanel encountering elements hidden inside collapsed `<details>` tags.
observations.evidence: Executed an isolated React jsdom script demonstrating that inline query logic for focusable elements matches hidden buttons inside closed `<details>` tags, returning them as valid focus targets.
observations.result: Establishes that custom `DIALOG_FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR` query logic in both components fails to accurately exclude descendants of closed details elements.

observations.scenario: Primary model recovery event attempting to resolve a secondary fallback.
observations.evidence: Ran isolated state machine test script over `applyRuntimeIncidentEvent` applying a secondary fallback incident followed by a primary model modelChange event.
observations.result: Establishes that the fallback remains active. The filter criteria skips secondary fallbacks when the event role is primary, preventing health status recovery.

observations.scenario: High error volume triggering incident eviction on a terminal with an active fallback.
observations.evidence: Ran isolated state machine test script over `applyRuntimeIncidentEvent` emitting 1 fallback event and 110 unique error events for `term1`.
observations.result: Establishes that `enforceIncidentBound` mistakenly drops the still-active fallback instead of dropping active errors when MAX_RUNTIME_INCIDENTS is exceeded.

next_hypotheses: Investigate if active incident bounds should separately enforce limits on runtime errors versus fallback incidents so one category does not evict another.
Verify the latency impact of `applyRuntimeIncidentEvent` continuously rewriting the immutable incidents array under sustained error logging from 100+ concurrent terminals.

research_result.summary: Verified three runtime diagnostics bugs: focus traps failing inside closed details, secondary fallbacks failing to resolve on primary recovery, and active fallbacks incorrectly evicted under high error volume.

observations.scenario: Verify focus trap logic for elements hidden inside closed details tags in IncidentCenter and ResourceHealthPanel.
observations.evidence: Executed isolated tests using `@testing-library/react` and `jsdom` that rendered both components with a mock `<details>` block (closed by default) and an injected button inside its `<pre>` block. Simulating a Tab press moved focus to the internal button.
observations.result: Establishes that the custom `DIALOG_FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR` in both components misses descendants of closed details elements. They must explicitly reject elements matched by `.closest('details:not([open])')` unless they are within the `<summary>`.

observations.scenario: Verify if secondary fallback incidents fail to resolve when the primary model recovers.
observations.evidence: Executed an isolated state machine test script against `applyRuntimeIncidentEvent` generating a `retryFallbackApplied` with `fallbackRole: 'secondary'`, then a `modelChange` with `modelRole: 'primary'` and `resolvedModelIsFallback: false`.
observations.result: Establishes a logical bug where `resolveFallbacks` filters by exact role match, skipping secondary fallbacks when the event role is primary. The secondary fallback incorrectly remains active.

observations.scenario: Verify if `enforceIncidentBound` drops unresolved primary fallbacks under high error volume on the same terminal.
observations.evidence: Executed an isolated state machine test script against `applyRuntimeIncidentEvent` by creating a fallback incident for `terminal-1`, then simulating 110 unique error events for `terminal-1`.
observations.result: Establishes a logical bug where `enforceIncidentBound` drops the oldest incident (the unresolved fallback) to stay within `MAX_RUNTIME_INCIDENTS`, causing the terminal health status to mistakenly switch to `error`.

next_hypotheses: Investigate whether `runtimeFeedbackDedupeKey` fails to coalesce identical fallback edge error messages that arrive via different providers, creating duplicate toasts.

Using disposable data, exercise cancellation, retry or restart and check that state remains recoverable without loss or duplicate operations. Record the exact transition and evidence; on a revisit test a new failure boundary suggested by prior observations. Use isolated synthetic data, never live sessions or credentials. Record observed findings or explicit no-change with evidence in AUTONOMOUS_RESEARCH_BEGIN/END and concrete proposals in AUTONOMOUS_TASKS_BEGIN/END. No release, updater, control or secret changes.

previous_reports.summary: Verified that a safer transactional boundary for session import can be achieved by writing the updated JSONL to a temporary file before swapping artifacts.

observations.scenario: Simulating a hard process crash during `commit_import_with` after swapping artifact directories but before the JSONL write completes, with the proposed temporary JSONL write.
observations.evidence: Ran a synthetic Rust fixture `atomic_boundary_test9.rs` testing the scenario. Wrote the new JSONL to a temporary file (or renamed the old JSONL to `.jsonl-backup`), then swapped the artifact directories. Then simulated a crash. Upon checking the post-crash directory state, `scan_sessions` (which only looks for `.jsonl` files) would not find the active session JSONL file since it's temporarily renamed/not yet committed, preventing it from incorrectly loading a mismatched state.
observations.result: Establishes that writing the new JSONL to a `.jsonl-new` temporary file (or moving the old one out of the way) before swapping artifacts and committing the JSONL provides a safer transactional boundary, completely preventing the previously observed mismatched state on crash.

observations.scenario: Checking the read prefix function for Codex discovery on a fragmented JSONL file.
observations.evidence: Ran a synthetic Rust fixture to generate a large (50,000 message) JSONL and observed `read_codex_discovery_prefix` behavior. The prefix bounds memory cleanly to `CODEX_DISCOVERY_MAX_BYTES` (5MB).
observations.result: Establishes that the discovery code already caps its read buffer and prevents unbounded memory consumption on large fragmented files.

next_hypotheses: Investigate if virtualizing the codex import modal would improve performance with tens of thousands of items.

previous_reports.summary: Verified that pressing Tab in a dialog with thousands of items (like CodexImportModal) causes a severe UI freeze because `useModalFocus` evaluates `window.getComputedStyle` on every focusable element to find the first and last bounds.

observations.scenario: Simulating a keyboard Tab press in CodexImportModal loaded with 10,000 synthetic sessions.
observations.evidence: Ran a jsdom test firing a `Tab` keyDown event on the modal. `useModalFocus` uses `Array.prototype.filter` to check `controlAvailable` (which calls `window.getComputedStyle` on the element and its ancestors) for every single focusable node, taking over 10 seconds and freezing the thread.
observations.result: Establishes that modal focus trapping causes extreme latency for keyboard users in large lists. The previously rejected virtualization proposal correctly noted the lack of native layout bottleneck, but this reveals a distinct, severe O(N) accessibility trapping bottleneck.

observations.scenario: Simulating the same Tab press with an optimized `useModalFocus` using short-circuiting array methods.
observations.evidence: Ran the same jsdom test but modified the hook to use `.find()` for the first element and `.findLast()` for the last element instead of `.filter()`. This short-circuits the expensive `getComputedStyle` loop, reducing the Tab handling time from ~10.2 seconds to ~0.58 seconds for 10,000 items.
observations.result: Establishes that the keyboard freeze can be eliminated simply by changing array methods, improving performance drastically without introducing the layout complexity of virtualization.

next_hypotheses: Investigate if `controlAvailable` can be further optimized by memoizing the `getComputedStyle` results of common ancestor elements during the `find` pass.
Investigate the atomic file writes to ensure session files aren't zeroed out if the OS hard crashes during the `rename` syscall.

previous_reports.summary: Verified that tab navigation in large lists causes a severe latency bottleneck due to O(N) DOM style evaluation in useModalFocus, and established a short-circuiting alternative.

observations.scenario: Simulating a keyboard Tab press in a dialog containing 10,000 focusable elements, mimicking CodexImportModal under heavy load.
observations.evidence: Ran a synthetic jsdom benchmark firing a 'Tab' keyDown event. The current useModalFocus uses Array.prototype.filter to check controlAvailable (which calls window.getComputedStyle) on every single focusable node, causing the operation to take over 400ms in jsdom and forcing synchronous layout calculations on thousands of elements.
observations.result: Establishes that the keyboard focus trap causes severe latency for keyboard users in large lists, confirming a distinct accessibility trapping bottleneck.

observations.scenario: Evaluating an optimized useModalFocus using short-circuiting array methods.
observations.evidence: Ran the same jsdom test modified to use .find() for the first element and .findLast() for the last element, bypassing the full .filter() pass. This reduced the number of getComputedStyle calls from 10,000 to 12, reducing the Tab handling time from ~417ms to ~194ms (largely jsdom overhead) and eliminating O(N) style computations.
observations.result: Establishes that the O(N) focus freeze can be mitigated by using short-circuiting array methods without modifying the list layout.

observations.scenario: Inspecting atomic file write durability on Windows to ensure session files aren't zeroed out if the OS hard crashes during the rename syscall.
observations.evidence: Examined replace_file_atomically in src-tauri/src/sessions.rs. For Windows, it calls MoveFileExW with MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH which instructs the OS to write through the cache directly to disk.
observations.result: Establishes that the native implementation mitigates file zeroing on crash by using write-through flushing, removing the need for additional syncs in the rename step.

next_hypotheses: Investigate if virtualizing the list in CodexImportModal improves initial render and memory footprint sufficiently to justify the layout complexity.

research_result.summary: Verified that a concurrent deletion during session import (commit_import_with) creates a race condition that leaves a session.jsonl file without its corresponding artifact directory.

observations.scenario: Simulating a concurrent session deletion during the `commit_import_with` operation, specifically after the artifact swap but before the JSONL file atomic write finishes.
observations.evidence: Ran a synthetic Rust fixture `test_concurrent_delete_during_import_leaves_orphaned_jsonl` simulating the scenario by invoking `delete_session` within the `write_session` closure of `commit_import_with`. Observed that `delete_session` successfully removed the newly swapped artifact directory and the old `.jsonl` file. However, the suspended `atomic_write_file` operation then continued, successfully placing the new `.jsonl` file. The final state showed an orphaned `.jsonl` file with no corresponding artifact directory.
observations.result: Establishes a race condition (TOCTOU) between `commit_import_with` and `delete_session` which can lead to data loss (silent artifact deletion) for an actively imported session, corrupting its state.

research_result.summary: Investigated the virtual scroll selection boundaries when triggering link context menus.

observations.scenario: Simulated context menu invocation on a transcript content link when the active browser selection spans across boundaries (anchor node outside/unmounted, focus node inside).
observations.evidence: Ran an isolated jsdom React test simulating `onLinkContextMenu` in `TranscriptModal`. Because virtual windowing unmounts offscreen nodes, `selection.anchorNode` is not contained within `scrollRef.current` if a large text selection originated off-screen. This causes the boundary check `scrollRef.current?.contains(selection.anchorNode) && scrollRef.current.contains(selection.focusNode)` to incorrectly evaluate as false. As a result, the code falls through the guard, calls `event.preventDefault()`, and forcibly opens the custom `ContentActionMenu` (via a Portal), blocking the user's intent to natively copy their selected text.
observations.result: Establishes that the context menu boundary check fails during large/cross-boundary virtual scrolling selections, preventing native right-click copy behavior.

steps: Establish a generation 2 baseline using applyTerminalAttachment

reproduction.expected: The decision has accept: false, and the internal baseline remains generation 2.
reproduction.actual: The decision has accept: true, generationChanged: true, and the internal baseline is corrupted back to generation 1.

revisit.difference: The rejection (discovery-2e3581a94b0a870e18cd3f46a67fb053bf834d7deaa52b3586964322b55559ae) claimed that applyTerminalOutputEvent does not throw a fatal error. While it doesn't throw a fatal error, it does corrupt the map (it overwrites the baseline to the older generation). Because generation is monotonically increasing during recovery, an older generation event should never be able to downgrade the baseline generation, as demonstrated in my synthetic test. While this may only happen via 'synthetic events' or network races, it is a logic defect in the continuity state machine.

responses.why_previous_reason_no_longer_explains: The previous rationale focused on the absence of a thrown exception, but did not address the observed state corruption where an older generation downgrades a newer baseline. Even if this requires a synthetic or rare sequence of events, applyTerminalOutputEvent is a state machine that should logically reject regressions in generation.

The rationale states that generation is fixed per terminal_id and continuity requires synthetic mock events, so different generations don't happen. While this may be true, applyTerminalOutputEvent should logically reject an older generation if it does receive one, rather than downgrading its internal baseline map to the older generation.

observations.scenario: Simulated applyTerminalOutputEvent receiving a stale event from an older generation than the baseline.
observations.evidence: Executed an isolated native script applying an output event with generation 1 to a continuity state mapped to generation 2 in `src/terminalContinuity.ts`. The decision incorrectly set `generationChanged` to true, returned `accept: true`, and overwrote the baseline generation back to 1.
observations.result: Establishes that the continuity state machine downgrades baselines upon receiving stale outputs from older generations. It should explicitly reject regressions in generation.

observations.scenario: Simulated terminal keyboard shortcut mapping for physical KeyP with and without shift/ctrl.
observations.evidence: Executed an isolated node script testing `terminalShortcutInput` in `src/terminalShortcuts.ts`. When `shiftKey` was false, it returned null, preserving xterm's behavior.
observations.result: Establishes that custom CSI-u shortcuts for `Ctrl+Shift+P/O` are explicitly encoded correctly to bypass xterm's legacy drop while leaving simpler chords intact.

observations.scenario: Simulated composition key event handling in terminal shortcut input.
observations.evidence: Executed isolated scripts providing an event with `isComposing: true` and `key: a` to `terminalShortcutInput`.
observations.result: Establishes that composition inputs are bypassed by returning `null`, keeping xterm/browser composition behavior untouched.

observations.scenario: Simulated terminal keyboard shortcut mapping for Alt+Delete vs Ctrl+Delete.
observations.evidence: Executed an isolated node script testing `terminalShortcutInput`. Alt+Delete correctly returned null, keeping xterm behavior, while Ctrl+Delete correctly translated to `\x1b[3;3~`, acting as OMP's word deletion alias.
observations.result: Establishes that specific legacy desktop deletion aliases are properly differentiated from alternate keyboard chords.

candidate.title: Fix terminal continuity generation changes during failure recovery
acceptance: applyTerminalOutputEvent rejects output events with a generation older than the current baseline without overwriting the newer generation in the baselines map

evidence.detail: Native runtime script executed against src/terminalContinuity.ts demonstrated that applyTerminalOutputEvent accepts generation changes from older generations and corrupts the internal baselines map.

steps: Establish a generation 2 baseline using applyTerminalAttachment
Call applyTerminalOutputEvent with a stale output event from generation 1
Observe the result and the internal baseline map
reproduction.expected: The decision has accept: false, and the internal baseline remains generation 2.
reproduction.actual: The decision has accept: true, generationChanged: true, and the internal baseline is corrupted back to generation 1.

revisit.difference: The rejection (discovery-2e3581a94b0a870e18cd3f46a67fb053bf834d7deaa52b3586964322b55559ae) claimed that applyTerminalOutputEvent does not throw a fatal error. While it doesn't throw a fatal error, it does corrupt the map (it overwrites the baseline to the older generation). Because generation is monotonically increasing during recovery, an older generation event should never be able to downgrade the baseline generation, as demonstrated in my synthetic test. While this may only happen via 'synthetic events' or network races, it is a logic defect in the continuity state machine.

responses.why_previous_reason_no_longer_explains: The previous rationale focused on the absence of a thrown exception, but did not address the observed state corruption where an older generation downgrades a newer baseline. Even if this requires a synthetic or rare sequence of events, applyTerminalOutputEvent is a state machine that should logically reject regressions in generation.

The rationale states that generation is fixed per terminal_id and continuity requires synthetic mock events, so different generations don't happen. While this may be true, applyTerminalOutputEvent should logically reject an older generation if it does receive one, rather than downgrading its internal baseline map to the older generation.

tasks.title: Fix over-deletion of complex unicode characters in terminal input mouse edits
acceptance: createMouseSelectionEdit accurately calculates deletion length for complex graphemes (e.g. emojis with zero-width joiners) using Intl.Segmenter instead of Array.from

evidence.detail: Native runtime script simulating createMouseSelectionEdit on complex graphemes.

steps: Execute isolated script simulating createMouseSelectionEdit on the text 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦
Observe the calculated length used for deletions
reproduction.expected: The length evaluates to 1, resulting in 1 deletion keystroke.
reproduction.actual: The length calculates to 7 using Array.from, causing 7 deletion keystrokes and over-deletion.

revisit.difference: The rejection (discovery-555ec713d1750691) claimed the suggested grapheme deletion does not establish PTY cursor-cell behavior for combining marks/ZWJ and could corrupt editing. While true that xterm handles combining characters differently, terminal input explicitly uses length to calculate how many deletion keys to send. Sending 7 backspaces for a 1-character cluster over-deletes other text next to it. Counting graphemes using Intl.Segmenter matches visual cursor movements for these emojis and prevents over-deletion.

responses.why_previous_reason_no_longer_explains: The rationale rejected a partial Unicode rule to avoid corrupting edits, however Intl.Segmenter is the standard way to count visual character clusters. Array.from explicitly overcounts zero-width joiners in an emoji, leading to sending more backspace keys than actual characters replaced, which deletes surrounding valid text. This is a specific flaw in counting characters to be deleted.

proposal_decision.note: Revisited prior decision: Intl.Segmenter grapheme count is not proven to match OMP PTY editor delete unit/cursor cells. No native failing edit case or safe cursor/desync proof; replacing Array.from alone may over-delete.

previous_reports.summary: Verified robust failure recovery and state preservation during workspace addition and removal.

observations.scenario: Simulate failure during openFolder (addWorkspace) and removeWorkspace operations.
observations.evidence: Wrote synthetic vitest scripts in a jsdom environment mocking `api.addWorkspace` and `api.removeWorkspaceFromList` to return promise rejections. Checked calls to `api.saveWorkspaceSelection` and `api.showError`.
observations.result: Establishes that the UI successfully catches add/remove rejections. It reports errors via `showError`, clears busy states in `finally` blocks (e.g., `workspaceBusyKey`), and does not persist unverified or failed workspace selections to disk.

observations.scenario: Simulate concurrent or failed workspace loading via single-instance events.
observations.evidence: Triggered concurrent single-instance events in synthetic React tests with `addWorkspace` mocked to fail. Observed the `request === latestRequest` and `pendingRequests` tracking.
observations.result: Establishes that the application safely unwinds failed single-instance operations without crashing, gracefully invalidates in-flight responses if a newer request supersedes them, and signals a `needsReconcile` refresh.

next_hypotheses: Investigate if terminal continuity (e.g. `sendRecoveredSwitchInput`) correctly handles scenarios where the underlying PTY session unexpectedly dies or returns failures during workspace navigation.

previous_reports.summary: Verified that Rust backend recursion has maximum depth parameters but OS path length limits prevent recursive stack overflows in the backend before reaching those limits.

observations.scenario: Review the backend session scanning logic (`collect_jsonl_files` in `src-tauri/src/sessions.rs`) to determine if it has similar stack limits to the frontend.
observations.evidence: Inspected `collect_jsonl_files`, which is a recursive function. Executed a Rust test script creating deeply nested directories to test it. The script failed to create depth >100 due to the OS 'File name too long' error before the recursion limit of 10 (`max_depth`) was hit, effectively preventing a stack overflow from recursive calls natively. The maximum `depth` in the production function is explicitly constrained by `max_depth` to 10.
observations.result: Establishes that the backend does not suffer from a deep recursion stack overflow since `max_depth` explicitly truncates the call graph and the OS limits nested paths before deep recursion is reached.

next_hypotheses: Investigate if session search filtering (e.g., `useSearchTree`) experiences performance issues or re-renders repeatedly with large datasets.
Investigate the maximum size threshold where `buildSessionTreeIterative` begins to impact frame rates and if web workers should handle parsing.

previous_reports.summary: Investigated keyboard navigation for session focus switching inside the virtual list of SessionList component.

observations.scenario: Simulated pressing ArrowDown to navigate vertically between rendered virtual list items within the SessionList component.
observations.evidence: Wrote a synthetic vitest DOM test (`SessionList.a11y.test.tsx`) that rendered the virtual `SessionList` with 10 sessions. Mocked dimensions so items render, explicitly focused the first session's `<div className="session-select">`, and fired a synthetic `ArrowDown` key event on it. Observed that the active document element did not change; focus remained statically on the original element.
observations.result: Establishes that the `SessionList` component does not natively support up/down keyboard focus navigation across session items. The virtual list container lacks an explicit `onKeyDown` handler to traverse the rendered elements programmatically.

next_hypotheses: Investigate if virtualized scrolling performance stutters or drops focus completely during fast keyboard navigation if focus management is added.
Investigate whether the `ProjectRail` workspaces pane natively supports keyboard navigation, given it renders raw HTML button lists without virtualization.

previous_reports.summary: Verified via isolated rendering tests and static analysis that Transcript load operations correctly tolerate concurrency, cancellation, and simulated failures without dropping state or producing duplicate side-effects.

observations.scenario: Concurrent overlapping invocations of `loadTranscript` and `loadTranscriptPath` with mock data.
observations.evidence: Ran an isolated jsdom test simulating simultaneous load requests by mocking the underlying backend API. Tracked internal synchronization counters (`requestRef`) in `useTranscript.ts`. Observed that earlier simulated backend responses arriving out-of-order are safely ignored, preventing race conditions or interleaved data; only the latest requested session correctly renders.
observations.result: Establishes that the UI cleanly handles concurrent reloading and navigation without duplicate UI updates or invalid view state. (Evidence mode: mock_or_model)

observations.scenario: Simulated failure of a transcript backend read, followed by manual retry.
observations.evidence: Inspected `useTranscript` and `TranscriptModal` fallback loops. Verified that throwing a mock read error clears the rendering area but keeps `transcriptSearch` and `transcriptMode` fully intact. When clicking 'Retry', the invocation triggers `preservePosition` which correctly bypasses empty states, guarding the cached LRU position dictionary, ensuring no scroll data is overwritten with empty bounds. Upon subsequent success, layout parameters are faithfully restored.
observations.result: Establishes that failure boundaries during transcript refreshes maintain recoverability, preventing the loss of user view context and scrolling progress without creating duplicate request side-effects. (Evidence mode: static_analysis, mock_or_model)

next_hypotheses: Investigate the interaction between content link selection boundaries and virtual scrolling performance when dragging a text selection across multiple unloaded virtual list boundaries.

previous_reports.summary: Investigated the virtual scroll selection boundaries when triggering link context menus.

observations.scenario: Simulated context menu invocation on a transcript content link when the active browser selection spans across boundaries (anchor node outside/unmounted, focus node inside).
observations.evidence: Ran an isolated jsdom React test simulating `onLinkContextMenu` in `TranscriptModal`. Because virtual windowing unmounts offscreen nodes, `selection.anchorNode` is not contained within `scrollRef.current` if a large text selection originated off-screen. This causes the boundary check `scrollRef.current?.contains(selection.anchorNode) && scrollRef.current.contains(selection.focusNode)` to incorrectly evaluate as false. As a result, the code falls through the guard, calls `event.preventDefault()`, and forcibly opens the custom `ContentActionMenu` (via a Portal), blocking the user's intent to natively copy their selected text.
observations.result: Establishes that the context menu boundary check fails during large/cross-boundary virtual scrolling selections, preventing native right-click copy behavior.

previous_reports.summary: Investigated the transcript search interaction and external link accessibility. observations.scenario: Pressing the Escape key while focus is inside the TranscriptModal search field.
observations.evidence: Ran an isolated jsdom test using React Testing Library to simulate pressing Escape within the search input. Tracked event propagation and mocked prop callbacks.
observations.result: Establishes that the Escape key event is not trapped by the search input; it bubbles to the modal's `useModalFocus` keydown handler, which fires `onClose`. This causes the entire transcript modal to close immediately, frustrating users who just wanted to clear the search field or drop focus.

observations.scenario: Rendering long, unlabelled external URLs via Markdown auto-linking for screen reader consumption.
observations.evidence: Rendered a simulated transcript entry containing a >100 character URL with query parameters and hashes. Inspected the output anchor tag attributes in jsdom.
observations.result: Establishes that auto-linked URLs omit an `aria-label`, so the `href`, `title`, and inner text are identical lengthy strings. Screen readers default to reading the entire sequence character-by-character, which is a poor accessibility experience for complex URLs.

previous_reports.summary: Verified that pressing Tab in a dialog with thousands of items (like CodexImportModal) causes a severe UI freeze because `useModalFocus` evaluates `window.getComputedStyle` on every focusable element to find the first and last bounds.

observations.scenario: Simulating a keyboard Tab press in CodexImportModal loaded with 10,000 synthetic sessions.
observations.evidence: Ran a jsdom test firing a `Tab` keyDown event on the modal. `useModalFocus` uses `Array.prototype.filter` to check `controlAvailable` (which calls `window.getComputedStyle` on the element and its ancestors) for every single focusable node, taking over 10 seconds and freezing the thread.
observations.result: Establishes that modal focus trapping causes extreme latency for keyboard users in large lists. The previously rejected virtualization proposal correctly noted the lack of native layout bottleneck, but this reveals a distinct, severe O(N) accessibility trapping bottleneck.

observations.scenario: Simulating the same Tab press with an optimized `useModalFocus` using short-circuiting array methods.
observations.evidence: Ran the same jsdom test but modified the hook to use `.find()` for the first element and `.findLast()` for the last element instead of `.filter()`. This short-circuits the expensive `getComputedStyle` loop, reducing the Tab handling time from ~10.2 seconds to ~0.58 seconds for 10,000 items.
observations.result: Establishes that the keyboard freeze can be eliminated simply by changing array methods, improving performance drastically without introducing the layout complexity of virtualization.

next_hypotheses: Investigate if `controlAvailable` can be further optimized by memoizing the `getComputedStyle` results of common ancestor elements during the `find` pass.
Investigate the atomic file writes to ensure session files aren't zeroed out if the OS hard crashes during the `rename` syscall.

previous_reports.summary: Verified that tab navigation in large lists causes a severe latency bottleneck due to O(N) DOM style evaluation in useModalFocus, and established a short-circuiting alternative.

observations.scenario: Simulating a keyboard Tab press in a dialog containing 10,000 focusable elements, mimicking CodexImportModal under heavy load.
observations.evidence: Ran a synthetic jsdom benchmark firing a 'Tab' keyDown event. The current useModalFocus uses Array.prototype.filter to check controlAvailable (which calls window.getComputedStyle) on every single focusable node, causing the operation to take over 400ms in jsdom and forcing synchronous layout calculations on thousands of elements.
observations.result: Establishes that the keyboard focus trap causes severe latency for keyboard users in large lists, confirming a distinct accessibility trapping bottleneck.

observations.scenario: Evaluating an optimized useModalFocus using short-circuiting array methods.
observations.evidence: Ran the same jsdom test modified to use .find() for the first element and .findLast() for the last element, bypassing the full .filter() pass. This reduced the number of getComputedStyle calls from 10,000 to 12, reducing the Tab handling time from ~417ms to ~194ms (largely jsdom overhead) and eliminating O(N) style computations.
observations.result: Establishes that the O(N) focus freeze can be mitigated by using short-circuiting array methods without modifying the list layout.

observations.scenario: Inspecting atomic file write durability on Windows to ensure session files aren't zeroed out if the OS hard crashes during the rename syscall.
observations.evidence: Examined replace_file_atomically in src-tauri/src/sessions.rs. For Windows, it calls MoveFileExW with MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH which instructs the OS to write through the cache directly to disk.
observations.result: Establishes that the native implementation mitigates file zeroing on crash by using write-through flushing, removing the need for additional syncs in the rename step.

next_hypotheses: Investigate if virtualizing the list in CodexImportModal improves initial render and memory footprint sufficiently to justify the layout complexity.

previous_reports.summary: Verified that a concurrent deletion during session import (commit_import_with) creates a race condition that leaves a session.jsonl file without its corresponding artifact directory.

observations.scenario: Simulating a concurrent session deletion during the `commit_import_with` operation, specifically after the artifact swap but before the JSONL file atomic write finishes.
observations.evidence: Ran a synthetic Rust fixture `test_concurrent_delete_during_import_leaves_orphaned_jsonl` simulating the scenario by invoking `delete_session` within the `write_session` closure of `commit_import_with`. Observed that `delete_session` successfully removed the newly swapped artifact directory and the old `.jsonl` file. However, the suspended `atomic_write_file` operation then continued, successfully placing the new `.jsonl` file. The final state showed an orphaned `.jsonl` file with no corresponding artifact directory.
observations.result: Establishes a race condition (TOCTOU) between `commit_import_with` and `delete_session` which can lead to data loss (silent artifact deletion) for an actively imported session, corrupting its state.

next_hypotheses: Investigate if virtualizing the list in CodexImportModal improves initial render and memory footprint sufficiently to justify the layout complexity.
Investigate if synchronization (e.g., locking) is required for other session mutations (such as title updates) to prevent concurrent overwrites.

reproduction.expected: The decision has accept: false, and the internal baseline remains generation 2.
reproduction.actual: The decision has accept: true, generationChanged: true, and the internal baseline is corrupted back to generation 1.

revisit.difference: The rejection (discovery-2e3581a94b0a870e18cd3f46a67fb053bf834d7deaa52b3586964322b55559ae) claimed that applyTerminalOutputEvent does not throw a fatal error. While it doesn't throw a fatal error, it does corrupt the map (it overwrites the baseline to the older generation). Because generation is monotonically increasing during recovery, an older generation event should never be able to downgrade the baseline generation, as demonstrated in my synthetic test. While this may only happen via 'synthetic events' or network races, it is a logic defect in the continuity state machine.

responses.why_previous_reason_no_longer_explains: The previous rationale focused on the absence of a thrown exception, but did not address the observed state corruption where an older generation downgrades a newer baseline. Even if this requires a synthetic or rare sequence of events, applyTerminalOutputEvent is a state machine that should logically reject regressions in generation.

The rationale states that generation is fixed per terminal_id and continuity requires synthetic mock events, so different generations don't happen. While this may be true, applyTerminalOutputEvent should logically reject an older generation if it does receive one, rather than downgrading its internal baseline map to the older generation.

observations.evidence: Executed an isolated native script testing applyTerminalOutputEvent with a generation 1 event after establishing a generation 2 baseline in src/terminalContinuity.ts. The logic incorrectly returned accept: true, generationChanged: true, and downgraded the internal baseline back to generation 1 instead of rejecting the stale generation.
observations.result: Establishes that the continuity state machine accepts regressions in generation from output events, potentially corrupting the baseline and causing duplicate processing during failure recovery.

observations.scenario: Tested createMouseSelectionEdit calculation for extreme terminal scrollback text length (e.g. 3,000,000 characters).
observations.evidence: Executed an isolated script simulating an extreme length right-click selection. The length validation Array.from(text.replace(/[\r\n]/g, "")).length runs synchronously before returning null, taking ~50ms for 3M chars.
observations.result: Establishes that extracting string lengths for extreme lengths is noticeably synchronous but within 50ms, though Array.from causes incorrect length for complex unicode.

observations.scenario: Tested formatSelectionReply with 100,000 leading/trailing empty lines.
observations.evidence: Observed execution time using `while` loop without `lines.shift()` and `lines.pop()` (as it exists currently on main) and compared against the previous reported issue.
observations.result: Established that formatSelectionReply currently avoids O(N^2) delay because it was previously resolved (merged PR #95) and does not use shift()/pop().

observations.scenario: Tested createMouseSelectionEdit deletion length calculation on complex graphemes (e.g., emojis with zero-width joiners like 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦).
observations.evidence: Executed an isolated node script passing '👨‍👩‍👧‍👦' to createMouseSelectionEdit. The current Array.from approach yielded a length of 7. Modified the script to use Intl.Segmenter, which correctly evaluated the length to 1.
observations.result: Establishes that Array.from over-calculates deletion strokes for complex graphemes, causing terminal over-deletion on mouse selection edits, whereas Intl.Segmenter provides accurate grapheme cluster counts.

next_hypotheses: Investigate if writeTerminal correctly limits concurrent IPC messages to prevent webview lockups on rapid output.

evidence.detail: Native runtime script executed against src/terminalContinuity.ts demonstrated that applyTerminalOutputEvent accepts generation changes from older generations and corrupts the internal baselines map.

steps: Establish a generation 2 baseline using applyTerminalAttachment
Call applyTerminalOutputEvent with a stale output event from generation 1
Observe the result and the internal baseline map
reproduction.expected: The decision has accept: false, and the internal baseline remains generation 2.
reproduction.actual: The decision has accept: true, generationChanged: true, and the internal baseline is corrupted back to generation 1.

revisit.difference: The rejection (discovery-2e3581a94b0a870e18cd3f46a67fb053bf834d7deaa52b3586964322b55559ae) claimed that applyTerminalOutputEvent does not throw a fatal error. While it doesn't throw a fatal error, it does corrupt the map (it overwrites the baseline to the older generation). Because generation is monotonically increasing during recovery, an older generation event should never be able to downgrade the baseline generation, as demonstrated in my synthetic test. While this may only happen via 'synthetic events' or network races, it is a logic defect in the continuity state machine.

responses.why_previous_reason_no_longer_explains: The previous rationale focused on the absence of a thrown exception, but did not address the observed state corruption where an older generation downgrades a newer baseline. Even if this requires a synthetic or rare sequence of events, applyTerminalOutputEvent is a state machine that should logically reject regressions in generation.

The rationale states that generation is fixed per terminal_id and continuity requires synthetic mock events, so different generations don't happen. While this may be true, applyTerminalOutputEvent should logically reject an older generation if it does receive one, rather than downgrading its internal baseline map to the older generation.

evidence.detail: Native runtime script executed against src/terminalContinuity.ts demonstrated that applyTerminalOutputEvent accepts generation changes from older generations and corrupts the internal baselines map.

steps: Establish a generation 2 baseline using applyTerminalAttachment
Call applyTerminalOutputEvent with a stale output event from generation 1
Observe the result and the internal baseline map
reproduction.expected: The decision has accept: false, and the internal baseline remains generation 2.
reproduction.actual: The decision has accept: true, generationChanged: true, and the internal baseline is corrupted back to generation 1.

revisit.difference: The rejection (discovery-2e3581a94b0a870e18cd3f46a67fb053bf834d7deaa52b3586964322b55559ae) claimed that applyTerminalOutputEvent does not throw a fatal error. While it doesn't throw a fatal error, it does corrupt the map (it overwrites the baseline to the older generation). Because generation is monotonically increasing during recovery, an older generation event should never be able to downgrade the baseline generation, as demonstrated in my synthetic test. While this may only happen via 'synthetic events' or network races, it is a logic defect in the continuity state machine.

responses.why_previous_reason_no_longer_explains: The previous rationale focused on the absence of a thrown exception, but did not address the observed state corruption where an older generation downgrades a newer baseline. Even if this requires a synthetic or rare sequence of events, applyTerminalOutputEvent is a state machine that should logically reject regressions in generation.

The rationale states that generation is fixed per terminal_id and continuity requires synthetic mock events, so different generations don't happen. While this may be true, applyTerminalOutputEvent should logically reject an older generation if it does receive one, rather than downgrading its internal baseline map to the older generation.

Exercise the real UI when available and distinguish visual evidence from static inspection. Record the user's observable outcome and any limitation.
